page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro System and built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by AWS Neoverse-V1 silicon operating at 2.6 GHz. Because each vCPU maps to a dedicated physical execution core without simultaneous multithreading, it eliminates thread-level resource contention. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 1900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Network throughput is provisioned at a 15 Gbps baseline, and there are no GPUs or hardware coprocessors included.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional throughput across the memory and multi-core execution subsystems. The server achieves top-tier results in PassMark memory testing, supported by strong uncached memory bandwidth measuring 246.48 GB/sec in sequential read operations and 104.75 GB/sec in write operations. Multi-core performance is strong, registering 17521.0 points in Geekbench multi-core testing and 31126.49 in PassMark database operations. Web throughput benchmarks show strong transfer rates reaching 49.3 GB/sec for static delivery. In contrast, single-thread metrics fall squarely within median industry distributions, and unaccelerated CPU processing for 70B parameter language models registers lower-tier throughput.

The qualitative efficiency profile of the c7gd.8xlarge centers on its dedicated Neoverse-V1 core density paired with high-speed local NVMe storage. Bundled fast storage combined with elevated memory bandwidth offers a balanced hardware footprint for high-IOPS applications without requiring external network-attached volumes. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation, distributed database engines, caching clusters, and high-concurrency web serving, while workloads demanding larger per-core RAM footprints or hardware matrix accelerators will require different hardware profiles.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 32-core AWS Neoverse-V1 ARMv8 processor running at 2.6 GHz. Utilizing the Nitro hypervisor architecture with dedicated physical cores and no simultaneous multithreading, it delivers 32 vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of memory for a compute-focused 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. The configuration includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 15 Gbps baseline network interface without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier memory subsystem throughput alongside strong Geekbench multi-core scores, high uncached memory bandwidth, and strong database transaction execution. Although single-threaded tasks and dense machine learning inference land within average or lower percentile bands, the hardware combination of dedicated compute and integrated high-speed local storage makes the c7gd.8xlarge suitable for distributed database nodes, high-concurrency web services, and parallel software build pipelines.
